I see the output sequence as swapping outermost and innermost colors while keeping the middle rings unchanged. from collections import deque

def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    out=[row[:] for row in grid]
    seen=set()
    for r in range(h):
      for c in range(w):
        if grid[r][c]==0 or (r,c) in seen: continue
        q=deque([(r,c)]); seen.add((r,c)); cells=[]
        while q:
          x,y=q.popleft(); cells.append((x,y))
          for dx,dy in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
            nx,ny=x+dx,y+dy
            if 0<=nx<h and 0<=ny<w and grid[nx][ny]!=0 and (nx,ny) not in seen:
              seen.add((nx,ny)); q.append((nx,ny))
        r0=min(x for x,y in cells); r1=max(x for x,y in cells)
        c0=min(y for x,y in cells); c1=max(y for x,y in cells)
        # Read the nested color sequence along the central vertical line.
        cmid=(c0+c1)//2
        seq=[]
        for x in range(r0,r1+1):
          v=grid[x][cmid]
          if v and (not seq or seq[-1]!=v): seq.append(v)
        # For concentric rectangular bands, sequence is outer-to-inner; reverse its colors.
        mapping={v:seq[-1-i] for i,v in enumerate(seq)}
        for x,y in cells:
          if grid[x][y] in mapping: out[x][y]=mapping[grid[x][y]]
    return out
